c.tagline: Music City, USA — honky-tonks, hot chicken, and nonstop live music.

taxi.fareNote: Traditional taxis are metered, but ride-hailing (Uber/Lyft) is far more common and usually cheaper; street-hailing is rare outside downtown.

emergency.note: 911 is the single nationwide emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across the US.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution a few blocks off Broadway at night; petty crime in nightlife

hood_desc: Neon-lit honky-tonks, live music from morning to night, and the Ryman Auditorium pack Lower Broadway; loud, touristy, and the epicenter of Music City nightlife.
A polished, walkable district of rooftop bars, upscale restaurants, boutiques, and the famous wings mural; nightlife and dining in a modern high-rise setting.
An artsy, bohemian enclave across the river with vintage shops, indie coffee, dive bars, and some of the city's most creative kitchens; the local hipster heartland.
Nashville's oldest neighborhood, now a quiet, historic pocket of red-brick townhomes, acclaimed farm-to-table restaurants, and the Nashville Farmers' Market.
A trendy, photogenic strip of boutiques, brunch spots, and murals popular for shopping and strolling; leafy and residential just off the main drag.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Buses generally run from about 5am to 11pm with reduced weekend frequency; the WeGo Star runs weekday peak hours only.
transit.pay: Buy fares in the WeGo app or pay cash on board (exact change). A local one-way bus ride is $2 and an all-day pass is $4. The WeGo Star commuter train to Lebanon has separate, zone-based fares.

transit.m: WeGo Route 18 airport bus to downtown (~30-45 min)

tip.r: ~15-20% at restaurants and bars is expected across the US; tipping is a core part of service workers' pay.

food.name: Nashville hot chicken
food.desc: Fried chicken painted with a cayenne-and-lard paste and served on white bread with pickles. Order one heat level below your ego.

places.name: Prince's Hot Chicken
places.note: The original, invented here; still the benchmark after 70-plus years.

places.name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken
places.note: The most accessible version, six heat levels and long queues.

places.name: Bolton's Spicy Chicken and Fish
places.note: Cult favourite, brutally hot and beloved by locals.

food.name: Meat-and-three
food.desc: Cafeteria-line Southern lunch: pick one meat and three vegetable sides, plus cornbread. The city's true everyday meal.

places.name: Arnold's Country Kitchen
places.note: James Beard-recognised institution; Monday is fried chicken day.

places.name: Swett's Restaurant
places.note: Family-run since 1954, a cornerstone of Black Nashville dining.

places.name: Monell's Dining and Country Store
places.note: Family-style at shared tables, passed around endlessly.

food.name: Buttermilk biscuits
food.desc: Tall, flaky Southern biscuits split for sausage gravy, country ham or a piece of fried chicken.

places.name: Loveless Cafe
places.note: Biscuits made from the same recipe since 1951, on the old Highway 100.

places.name: Biscuit Love
places.note: Modern biscuit house famous for the fried-biscuit Bonuts.

places.name: Nashville Biscuit House
places.note: Plain diner doing the unglamorous, excellent original.

food.name: Tennessee barbecue
food.desc: Pork shoulder smoked over hickory, pulled and dressed with vinegar sauce; whole-hog and dry-rubbed ribs both have a following.

places.name: Martin's Bar-B-Que Joint
places.note: Whole-hog pit barbecue and the outsized redneck taco.

places.name: Peg Leg Porker
places.note: Memphis-style dry ribs from a Nashville barbecue name.

places.name: Edley's Bar-B-Que
places.note: Neighbourhood standby for brisket, pulled pork and sides.

food.name: Hot fish
food.desc: Cornmeal-fried whiting stacked on white bread with hot sauce and slaw - the older, less-hyped sibling of hot chicken.

places.name: Bolton's Spicy Chicken and Fish
places.note: Fish is arguably better than the chicken and just as fiery.

places.name: Ed's Fish House
places.note: No-frills fish house serving the North Nashville fry tradition.

places.name: Prince's Hot Chicken
places.note: Fried fish plates alongside the famous chicken.

food.name: Banana pudding
food.desc: Vanilla custard layered with wafers and bananas under whipped cream or meringue - the default Southern dessert.

places.name: Loveless Cafe
places.note: Every component made in house; the version most often cited as best.

places.name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken
places.note: The cooling side that makes the hot chicken survivable.

places.name: Arnold's Country Kitchen
places.note: Meat-and-three pudding, made daily and gone by early afternoon.

food.name: Tennessee whiskey
food.desc: Charcoal-mellowed sour-mash whiskey; Nashville distilleries have revived the pre-Prohibition Green Brier style.

places.name: Nelson's Green Brier Distillery
places.note: Family-revived 19th-century whiskey brand with tastings and tours.

places.name: Corsair Distillery
places.note: Experimental small-batch whiskeys and a taproom.

places.name: Robert's Western World
places.note: Honky-tonk institution; whiskey, a longneck and free live country.

food.name: Sweet tea
food.desc: Black tea brewed strong and sweetened while hot, served over ice by the pitcher. The unofficial house wine of the South.

places.name: Arnold's Country Kitchen
places.note: Refilled constantly with the meat-and-three plate.

places.name: Loveless Cafe
places.note: Sweet tea by the glass with biscuits and country ham.

places.name: Monell's Dining and Country Store
places.note: Pitchers on the table as part of the family-style service.

landmarks: The Parthenon
A full-scale replica of the ancient Athenian temple standing in Centennial Park, complete with a towering gilded statue of Athena inside.
Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
An architecturally striking museum shaped like a piano keyboard and radio tower, chronicling country music's biggest legends.
Ryman Auditorium
The 'Mother Church of Country Music,' a red-brick 1892 tabernacle-turned-concert-hall famed for its stained glass and legendary stage.
Lower Broadway
Nashville's neon-lit honky-tonk strip packed with live music venues, boot shops, and the buzzing energy that defines Music City.
Grand Ole Opry House
The famous home of the world's longest-running live radio broadcast, a must-see shrine for country music fans.
Tennessee State Capitol
A stately Greek Revival capitol building perched atop a hill in downtown Nashville, offering commanding city views.
AT&T Building ('Batman Building')
Nashville's tallest skyscraper, nicknamed for its twin spires that resemble bat ears, dominating the downtown skyline.
Johnny Cash Museum
An immersive downtown museum dedicated to the Man in Black, showcasing memorabilia from his legendary career.
Cheekwood Estate & Gardens
A grand historic mansion surrounded by sprawling botanical gardens and art installations, a peaceful contrast to downtown's buzz.
Bridgestone Arena
The home of the Nashville Predators and a major concert venue, its marquee lights up the heart of downtown.

train.note: Nashville has no Amtrak service at all - Tennessee's only passenger train is the WeGo Star, a 32-mile commuter line with seven stations running from Riverfront station downtown out to Lebanon, and it operates on weekday peaks only over a mostly single-track route. To reach the national network you have to travel to Memphis for the City of New Orleans (about three hours west) or Atlanta for the Crescent (roughly four hours southeast). No international trains exist anywhere in the region. In practice, leaving Nashville means a coach, a car or a flight.

bus.note: There are no international coaches from Nashville. Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/), FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and Megabus (https://us.megabus.com/) cover the long-distance market from the downtown bus station and nearby curbside stops, with roughly three and a half hours to Memphis, three to Louisville, four and a half to Atlanta, three to Knoxville and five to St Louis. Tickets are bought online and are considerably cheaper booked a week or more ahead. WeGo Public Transit (https://www.wegotransit.com/) runs the local buses that connect the terminal with downtown hotels.

ferry.note: Nashville sits on the Cumberland River but has no scheduled ferry service; the river is used by barges and by tourist boats such as the General Jackson showboat and riverfront sightseeing cruises. The city is around 400 miles from the Gulf coast, so there is no coastal or international option.

half.name: Franklin
half.blurb: A historic small town south of Nashville with a preserved downtown square and Civil War-era battlefield sites.

half.name: Leiper's Fork
half.blurb: A rural village of art galleries, antique shops, and a general store, home to several country music songwriters.

half.name: Lynchburg (Jack Daniel's Distillery)
half.blurb: A small Tennessee town built around the Jack Daniel's whiskey distillery, which offers tours of its production process.

full.name: Chattanooga
full.blurb: A city on the Tennessee River with the Lookout Mountain incline railway and Rock City rock-garden trails.
